review_notes: I read the whole file and the Nerve.lean companion. I searched the repository for uses of the `_comp` and `_id` lemmas. There are no uses outside the file itself, so the finding rests on the visible asymmetry in the simp set and not on a downstream use. The rfl lemmas `_X`, `_vertical`, `_δ`, `_d` and `_def` are plain unfolding lemmas on abbrevs/defs. Leaving them non-simp looks intentional, and I did not flag them. The `@[simp]` lemmas `_f`, `_f_zero`, `_id` and `_inclusion` look correctly oriented. I did not check for loops because the rewrites go from a map to a more primitive map and cannot feed back into themselves. I could not run Lean. I have not confirmed that simp would unify the proof-term argument `fun i _ hx => ...` in the `_comp` statements, though it should by proof irrelevance.

findings.excerpt: theorem openCoverSingularBicomplexMap_comp {Y Z : TopCat.{u}} {κ τ : Type u}
findings.problem: The functoriality lemmas are only half exposed to simp. `openCoverSingularBicomplexMap_id` and `openCoverSingularTotalMap_id` are `@[simp]`, but the matching `_comp` lemmas (also the one at line 232) are not. An expression like `openCoverSingularTotalMap U R W (f ≫ g) (s ∘ r) _` therefore cannot be normalised to `openCoverSingularTotalMap U R V f r hf ≫ openCoverSingularTotalMap V R W g s hg`. The `_inclusion` simp lemma has the same limitation: it fires only when the map is already stated at a fixed `f`. The `_comp` lemmas are the only way to split such a composite, and they must be applied by hand. This leaves the simp interface uneven. The same pattern appears in `openCoverArrowMap_comp` in Nerve.lean, where `_id` is `@[simp]` and `_comp` is not.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `openCoverSingularBicomplexMap_comp` and `openCoverSingularTotalMap_comp` with `@[simp]` (and `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` if they are used in categorical chains). The direction is already right: the left side is one map of a composite, and the right side is a composite of two maps. The right side has strictly smaller arguments, so it cannot loop. If the maintainers want `s ∘ r` kept as the normal form of the cover reindexing, keep the `_comp` lemmas non-simp and say so in the docstring.
findings.benefit: Proofs about composites of cover maps (for example naturality or descent arguments) could be closed with `simp`, as is already possible for identities. The simp-set would be consistent with the `_id` lemmas.
